cards.front: What are the three ways to read a road sign?
cards.back: By its shape, its colour and the message printed on it. Understanding these three ways of classifying signs helps you figure out the meaning of signs that are new to you.

cards.front: What are regulatory signs, and what happens if you disregard one?
cards.back: Regulatory signs tell you about driving laws and regulations. It is an offence under the B.C. Motor Vehicle Act to disregard them, and drivers who don't follow their instructions may receive penalties. Examples include stop, yield, speed limit, do not enter, one way, keep right, no stopping and no-passing signs.

cards.front: What do a stop sign and a yield sign require you to do?
cards.back: Stop sign (a red octagon): stop completely and continue only when safe. Yield sign (a downward-pointing triangle): give the right-of-way to other vehicles and crossing pedestrians.

cards.front: What does a posted speed limit sign mean?
cards.back: It shows the maximum legal speed when the road is bare and dry and visibility is good. A separate sign can indicate that a lower speed limit is ahead.

cards.front: What colour are school zone signs, and when is a school zone speed tab in effect?
cards.back: School zone signs are fluorescent yellow-green. If the tab underneath only indicates the speed limit, that limit is in effect from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on school days. The tab may also state its own hours (for example, a 30 km/h limit in effect 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on school days).

cards.front: When is a playground zone speed limit in effect?
cards.back: A playground zone's 30 km/h limit is in effect every day from dawn to dusk. A separate 'playground nearby' warning sign means be prepared to slow down.

cards.front: Where are lane use signs mounted, and what must you do in a designated lane?
cards.back: Lane use signs are mounted above the lane, or at the side of the lane before the intersection. If you're in a designated lane you must follow the direction indicated by the arrows, and you may not move into or out of a designated lane while you are in an intersection.

cards.front: What is the difference between a lane use sign and a turn control sign?
cards.back: Lane use signs are mounted above or beside the lane before the intersection and show which lanes may be used to turn or go straight. Turn control signs are mounted directly above the intersection, and you must follow the direction of the arrow.

A white diamond painted on the road surface marks reserved lanes, with thick solid or broken lines. Reserved lane signs are also placed over or beside lanes reserved for certain vehicles such as buses or high occupancy vehicles (HOVs); other HOV signs may state how many people must be in the vehicle.

cards.front: What shape and colour are most warning signs, and what are object markers?
cards.back: Most warning signs are yellow and diamond-shaped — they warn of possible hazards ahead (curves, steep hills, merging traffic, slippery road, etc.). Object markers are mounted on obstructions and tell you to keep right, keep left, or keep right or left.

cards.front: What do the three lane control signals mean?
cards.back: Green arrow: drive in this lane. Red X: do not drive in this lane. Yellow X: move out of this lane and into a lane with a green arrow — but if the lane control signals over all of the lanes are flashing yellow, slow down and proceed with caution.

cards.front: What do flashing red, flashing yellow and flashing green traffic lights mean?
cards.back: Flashing red: stop, then continue only when it is safe. Flashing yellow: slow down and proceed with caution. Flashing green: a pedestrian-controlled light — go only if the intersection is clear.

cards.front: What can you do at a steady red light? At a flashing green arrow with a steady red light?
cards.back: Steady red: stop — after coming to a full stop you may turn right, or turn left onto a one-way street, unless a sign forbids it. Flashing green arrow with steady red: a left turn is allowed, but through traffic must stop for the red light.

cards.front: What do yellow lines and white lines on the road each separate?
cards.back: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions — if there's a yellow line to your left, oncoming traffic is on the other side of it. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and also mark crosswalks, stopping positions and the right shoulders of highways.

cards.front: What do the different yellow line patterns allow?
cards.back: Broken line: passing is allowed when safe. Single yellow line: passing is allowed with extra caution. Broken line beside a solid line: you may pass only when it's safe and the broken line is on your side. Double solid line: no passing allowed. Double broken yellow line: the lane is reversible — a lane control signal shows whether you may use it.

cards.front: What is a two-way left-turn lane and a painted island?
cards.back: A two-way left-turn lane is shared by drivers travelling in opposite directions for left turns (the markings may be reversed — solid lines inside the broken lines). A painted island must be kept to your right — do not drive on or over it.

questions.q: Disregarding a regulatory sign, such as a stop or speed limit sign, is:
choices: An offence under the B.C. Motor Vehicle Act that may bring penalties
Only a problem if a crash results
A matter left to each municipality's discretion
Legal for commercial vehicles with a permit
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell you about driving laws and regulations, and it is an offence under the B.C. Motor Vehicle Act to disregard them.

questions.q: A posted maximum speed limit sign applies when:
choices: Traffic is light, regardless of weather
The road is bare and dry and visibility is good
You are driving downhill
It is raining or snowing
questions.explanation: The speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed when the road is bare and dry and visibility is good — in poorer conditions you should drive slower.

questions.q: An eight-sided red sign requires you to:
choices: Slow down and yield to traffic on your left
Sound your horn before proceeding
Stop completely and continue only when safe
Stop only if other vehicles are approaching
questions.explanation: A stop sign means stop completely — continue only when safe. A yield sign, by contrast, means give the right-of-way to other vehicles and crossing pedestrians.

questions.q: A rectangular regulatory sign showing a snowflake and tire symbols means:
choices: Slippery road ahead
Snow plows may be working ahead
Chains are never required on this route
Winter tires or chains must be used when the sign is displayed
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign means winter tires or chains must be used when the sign is displayed.

questions.q: School zone signs are what colour?
choices: Fluorescent yellow-green
Orange
Blue and white
Red and white
questions.explanation: School zone signs (and the school crosswalk ahead warning sign) are fluorescent yellow-green.

questions.q: A school zone sign has a tab underneath showing only a speed limit. When is that limit in effect?
choices: 24 hours a day, every day
From 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on school days
From dawn to dusk every day
Only when children are visible
questions.explanation: If the tab under a school zone sign only indicates the speed limit, that limit is in effect from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on school days.

questions.q: When is a playground zone's 30 km/h speed limit in effect?
choices: From 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on school days
Only on weekends and holidays
Every day from dawn to dusk
Only when the playground is occupied
questions.explanation: A playground zone's 30 km/h limit is in effect every day from dawn to dusk — unlike a school zone tab, which applies from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on school days.

questions.q: You are driving in a lane marked by a lane use sign. While in the intersection, you may:
choices: Move out of the designated lane if you signal first
Change lanes if no vehicle is beside you
Move into a designated lane to turn
Not move into or out of the designated lane
questions.explanation: If you're in a designated lane you must follow the direction indicated by the arrows, and you may not move into or out of a designated lane while you are in an intersection.

questions.q: Where are turn control signs mounted?
choices: Directly above the intersection
At the side of the road well before the intersection
On the far curb beyond the intersection
On the pavement surface
questions.explanation: Turn control signs are mounted directly above the intersection and you must follow the direction of the arrow. Lane use signs, by contrast, are mounted above or beside the lane before the intersection.

questions.q: A lane reserved for certain vehicles such as buses or HOVs is marked on the road surface with:
choices: A yellow zigzag line
A white diamond
A red square
Double solid white lines only
questions.explanation: A white diamond painted on the road surface marks reserved lanes; HOV lanes are marked with thick solid or broken lines and white diamond symbols, and signs state which vehicles may use the lane.

questions.q: Most warning signs, which alert you to possible hazards ahead, are:
choices: Green and rectangular
Red and octagonal
Yellow and diamond-shaped
Blue and square
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are yellow and diamond-shaped. They warn of possible hazards ahead such as curves, merging traffic, steep hills and slippery roads.

questions.q: A yellow diamond-shaped sign showing a truck on a sloped ramp means:
choices: Truck parking area ahead
Trucks must use the left lane
Weigh scale ahead
Steep hill ahead — slow down
questions.explanation: This warning sign means a steep hill is ahead and you should slow down — especially important for heavy commercial vehicles.

questions.q: Object markers with striped panels are mounted on:
choices: Obstructions, showing you to keep right or left
School buses
Slow-moving vehicles
Railway crossing gates only
questions.explanation: Object markers are mounted on obstructions — pay special attention to them. Depending on the marker, keep right, keep left, or keep right or left.

questions.q: In a construction zone you must:
choices: Pass equipment closely so traffic keeps moving
Obey traffic-control persons, travel within the posted speed, stay well back from equipment and pass only when safe
Follow normal highway speed limits at all times
Ignore the signs when no workers are visible
questions.explanation: Construction signs warn of construction and maintenance work. You must obey traffic-control persons, travel within the posted speed, stay well back from all equipment and pass only when it is safe.

questions.q: At a railway crossing with a lowered gate, you must stay stopped until:
choices: The train has passed the crossing
The lights stop flashing, even if the gate is still moving
The gate is fully raised
Ten seconds have passed
questions.explanation: At a railway crossing you must stay stopped until the gate is fully raised. Remember, you must always yield to trains.

questions.q: A yellow X lane control signal is displayed over your lane, and the signals over all lanes are flashing yellow. You should:
choices: Stop immediately in your lane
Speed up to clear the lane
Treat it the same as a red X
Slow down and proceed with caution
questions.explanation: A yellow X means move into a lane with a green arrow — but when the lane control signals over all of the lanes are flashing yellow, slow down and proceed with caution. A red X means do not drive in that lane.

questions.q: After coming to a full stop at a steady red light, you may:
choices: Turn right, or turn left onto a one-way street, unless a sign forbids it
Proceed straight through if the intersection is clear
Turn left onto a two-way street
Not turn in any direction until the light turns green
questions.explanation: At a steady red light you must stop; after a full stop you may turn right or turn left onto a one-way street unless a sign forbids it.

questions.q: What does a flashing green light at an intersection mean?
choices: An advance left turn is coming
It is a pedestrian-controlled light — go only if the intersection is clear
The light is about to turn yellow
Buses only may proceed
questions.explanation: A flashing green light is a pedestrian-controlled light — go only if the intersection is clear. A flashing red means stop and continue only when safe; a flashing yellow means slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.q: You face a flashing green arrow together with a steady red light. What is permitted?
choices: All traffic may proceed with caution
Nothing — all traffic must remain stopped
A left turn is allowed; through traffic must stop for the red light
Right turns only
questions.explanation: A flashing green arrow with a steady red light allows the left turn shown by the arrow, while through traffic must stop for the red light.

questions.q: A steady white rectangular light at an intersection signal means:
choices: All vehicles may proceed straight through
The signal is out of order — treat as a four-way stop
Pedestrians only may cross
It is a transit priority signal — only buses may go on this signal
questions.explanation: The steady white rectangular light is a transit priority signal — only buses may go on this signal.

questions.q: What colour are the lines that divide traffic moving in opposite directions?
choices: Yellow
White
Orange
Red
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions — if there's a yellow line to your left, oncoming traffic is on the other side of it. White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

questions.q: The centre of the road is marked with a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line. You may pass:
choices: Never, in either direction
Only when it is safe and the broken line is on your side
Whenever the solid line is on your side
Only between dawn and dusk
questions.explanation: With a broken line and a solid line, you may pass only when it is safe and the broken line is on your side. A double solid yellow line means no passing is allowed.

questions.q: A lane marked on both sides by double broken yellow lines is:
choices: A bus-only lane
A painted island — do not drive on it
A reversible lane — a lane control signal shows whether you may use it
A two-way left-turn lane
questions.explanation: A double broken yellow line marks a reversible lane; the lane control signal will show whether you may use the lane. A two-way left-turn lane is shared by opposite directions for left turns.

questions.q: A solid white line between lanes of traffic travelling in the same direction means:
choices: Lane changing is encouraged
The lane is reserved for HOVs
The lane ends ahead
Do not change lanes
questions.explanation: A solid white line means do not change lanes; a broken white line means lane changing is allowed when safe.

questions.q: In a bicycle lane, marked with an outline of a bicycle, cyclists must:
choices: Travel in the same direction as the traffic beside them
Ride facing oncoming traffic
Yield to vehicles entering the lane
Dismount at every intersection
questions.explanation: A bicycle lane is for cyclists only, and cyclists must travel in the same direction as the traffic beside them. The lane is marked with an outline of a bicycle and sometimes with a diamond.

questions.q: When you approach a painted island on the roadway, you must:
choices: Drive over it only when turning left
Keep to the right and not drive on or over it
Stop before it and yield
Use it as a passing lane when clear
questions.explanation: Keep to the right of a painted island and do not drive on or over it. Also note it is illegal to drive over freshly painted, wet pavement markings.
